blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how your radio picks up signals or how doctors can see inside your body without surgery? The answers lie in the electromagnetic spectrum.

blocks.markdown: The electromagnetic spectrum is a range of all types of electromagnetic radiation. Radiation is energy that travels and spreads out as it goes. The types of radiation that make up the electromagnetic spectrum are, in order of increasing frequency: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays.

blocks.title: Electromagnetic Spectrum
blocks.text: The electromagnetic spectrum is the range of all types of electromagnetic radiation, arranged by frequency or wavelength.

blocks.markdown: All electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light in a vacuum, which is approximately $3 \times 10^8$ meters per second. Each region of the spectrum has different uses based on its properties.

items: Radio waves: Used for communication such as broadcasting radio and television.
Microwaves: Used in microwave ovens and for satellite communications.
Infrared: Used in remote controls and thermal imaging.
Visible light: The only part of the spectrum visible to the human eye.
Ultraviolet: Used in sterilizing medical equipment and in black lights.
X-rays: Used in medical imaging to view the inside of the body.
Gamma rays: Used in cancer treatment and to sterilize medical equipment.

blocks.title: Identifying Uses of EM Waves
blocks.prompt: What are some common uses of radio waves, X-rays, and gamma rays?

steps.text: Radio waves are commonly used for communication purposes. They are used in broadcasting radio and television signals.
X-rays are used in medical imaging to view the inside of the human body, such as checking for broken bones.
Gamma rays are used in the treatment of cancer, as they can kill cancerous cells.

blocks.answer: Radio waves are used for communication, X-rays for medical imaging, and gamma rays for cancer treatment.

blocks.markdown: Understanding the electromagnetic spectrum is crucial for many technological and medical applications. Each type of wave has unique properties that make it suitable for specific uses.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember the order of the electromagnetic spectrum by the acronym: RMIVUXG (Radio, Microwave, Infrared, Visible, Ultraviolet, X-ray, Gamma).

points: The electromagnetic spectrum includes radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays.
All electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light in a vacuum.
Different regions of the spectrum have different uses, such as communication, medical imaging, and cancer treatment.
